research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Follows Bloodsworth's journey from death row to exoneration to becoming an advocate for criminal justice reform. Available via CNN/Max.
research_notes_other.research_findings: Kirk Bloodsworth's case is landmark as the first US death row DNA exoneration. He was convicted based on eyewitness accounts despite lack of physical evidence, had his first conviction overturned due to prosecutorial misconduct (withheld evidence), was reconvicted, and finally freed by DNA testing in 1993. While a specific CNN Special Report titled "Sole Survivor" wasn't confirmed via search, his story has been widely covered, including in the 2015 documentary "Bloodsworth: An Innocent Man".

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Rape and Murder (of 9-year-old Dawn Hamilton in 1984)
featured_individuals.sentence: Death Penalty (first trial), Two Life Terms (second trial)
contributing_factors_raw: Eyewitness misidentification (multiple witnesses), withheld exculpatory evidence (led to first conviction being overturned)
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated by DNA evidence; Pardoned; Actual perpetrator identified via DNA in 2003
organizations_involved_raw: Innocence Project (assisted with DNA); Became advocate with Witness to Innocence.
